newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on sluggish demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on sluggish demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed mixed in continued sluggish trading due to absence of consumer demand, traders said.

"People are watching the Thai market where latex price has gone up. The local price may also go up but the question is whether demand will come in. So far there's no sign of buyers returning to the market," said one local trader.
"Nobody seems to be short at the moment," another trader said.
Traders said there was still ample supply of raw materials despite production being affected by wintering.
At the close, April RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 305 cents ($1.23) a kg, up one cent from Tuesday.
April SMR 20 buyer was down one cent at 293.50 ($1.19).
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 292 cents a kg, SMR CV at 357, SMR L at 337, SMR 5 at 304, SMR 10 at 293 and drum latex FOB at 237.
The INRO five-day moving average was 232.53 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Mar 11 against 232.61 on Mar 10. The daily indicator price was 232.35 versus 233.07.
